mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt 1ND-TV engine for your Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D typically costs £1,800-£2,200 supply-only, with used engines available from £800-£1,400. Fitting adds approximately £520-£650 for indie labour (8-10 hours at £65/hr). Used 1ND-TV: £800-£1,400. Reconditioned: £1,500-£2,000. Rebuilt with warranty: £1,800-£2,200. Supply & fit total: from around £1,300 for a used unit, up to £2,800+ for a rebuilt engine fitted.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of 1ND-TV engine failure in a Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most frequently reported issues across the Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D range are: rough idling, power loss and poor fuel economy from EGR valve clogging; rough running, hard starting and fuel system overpressure (P1229) from injector or pump wear; and gradual coolant loss without visible leaks from EGR cooler failure. Early warning signs include reduced power, hesitation on acceleration, increased fuel consumption and the Check Engine light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on your car's condition and value. A typical 2007-2018 Auris 1.4 D-4D is worth £1,500-£5,000 depending on condition and mileage. If your car is worth under £2,000: a used engine (£800-£1,400 fitted) or targeted repair is usually the better financial decision. If your car is worth over £3,000: a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty and upgraded components is a sound investment. If the car has sentimental value or you plan to keep it long-term: the warranty and reliability of a rebuilt unit often justifies the premium.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D engine replacement takes 1-2 working days at a specialist workshop (8-10 hours labour). Allow additional time for parts delivery if your chosen engine isn't in stock locally.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D and the 2.0 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.4 D-4D (1ND-TV) and 2.0 D-4D (1AD-FTV / 2AD-FTV) share Toyota's D-4D common-rail diesel architecture but differ significantly. 1.4 D-4D (1ND-TV): 1,364cc, 90hp, 205Nm, simpler SOHC design, no DPF on early models. 2.0 D-4D (1AD-FTV): 1,998cc, 124hp, 310Nm, more complex DOHC design, DPF-equipped. The 1.4 D-4D is simpler, more fuel-efficient and generally has fewer emissions-related issues than the larger 2.0 D-4D, making it a popular choice for budget-conscious buyers.

mainEntity.name: Is the Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D ULEZ compliant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1ND-TV engine in the Auris 1.4 D-4D meets Euro 4 (pre-2010) or Euro 5 (2010-2018) emissions standards depending on year. For London ULEZ: Euro 4 diesel (pre-2010) is NOT ULEZ compliant. Euro 5 diesel (2010-2015) is NOT ULEZ compliant. Euro 6 diesel (2015-2018) IS ULEZ compliant. Always check your vehicle's compliance using its registration number, as individual vehicle status can vary. If you drive in ULEZ zones regularly, consider a hybrid or petrol alternative.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 1.4 D-4D brought Toyota's common-rail diesel technology to the Auris range, offering a fuel-efficient and torquey alternative to the petrol engines. Powered exclusively by the 1ND-TV engine, it delivered 90hp and strong low-end pulling power ideal for urban and motorway driving.

milestones.description: 1.4 D-4D introduced with first-generation Auris (E150); 1ND-TV 1.4-litre common-rail diesel, 90hp, five-speed manual transmission
Facelift; 1.4 D-4D continues with emissions updates
Second-generation Auris (E180) launched; 1ND-TV engine carries over with Euro 5 emissions compliance
Business Edition trim introduced with 1.4 D-4D option
1.4 D-4D phased out as Auris replaced by Corolla; production ends December 2018

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 1ND-TV engine powering the Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D is a robust and fuel-efficient diesel unit - many have covered 150,000+ miles with proper maintenance. However, age and mileage bring three well-documented failure patterns. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: EGR Valve Clogging - Why the Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D 1ND-TV Loses Power
problems.rootCause: Like many modern diesels, the EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) valve can become clogged with soot buildup over time. This restricts airflow, causing rough idling, reduced power, poor fuel economy and potentially triggering the Check Engine light.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve, intake and throttle body
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for first occurrence; may need repeating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR valve with new OEM or quality aftermarket unit
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if cleaning doesn't resolve the fault

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £1,800-£2,200 (matches Section 4 rebuilt figure for this code)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit complete engine with new EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if EGR failure has caused related damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2007-2018 Auris 1.4 D-4D is worth approximately £1,500-£5,000 depending on condition, mileage and trim. With rebuilt engine supply costs starting around £1,800-£2,200, replacement cost may represent 40-100% of vehicle value on lower-value examples. For cars worth under £2,000, EGR cleaning or replacement is often the more financially sensible route.
problems.recommendation: Start with EGR cleaning - it's inexpensive and often resolves the issue. If the fault returns within 12 months, replace the EGR valve. Regular motorway driving helps reduce soot buildup, while short urban trips accelerate EGR clogging.
problems.cta: -> Compare Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D EGR repair costs

problems.h4: Fuel System & Injector Issues - Why the Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D 1ND-TV Suffers from Rough Running
problems.rootCause: The 1ND-TV's common-rail fuel system can develop issues, particularly fuel system overpressure (fault code P1229). This is often caused by high-pressure pump wear or injector degradation. Fuel system contamination can spread debris throughout the system, requiring extensive repair.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Professional cleaning, flow testing and nozzle replacement
Replace all four injectors with new or reconditioned units; includes coding
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution for injector-related issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace CP3 high-pressure pump; flush entire fuel system
repairOptions.longevity: Required if pump has failed and contaminated the system

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £1,800-£2,200 (matches Section 4 rebuilt figure for this code)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit complete engine with new fuel system components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if pump failure has caused widespread system damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For an Auris 1.4 D-4D worth £1,500-£5,000, injector replacement at £700-£1,200 is a significant but often worthwhile investment if the car is otherwise sound. If the high-pressure pump has failed and contaminated the entire fuel system, a full engine replacement with new fuel system components may be the most cost-effective solution.
problems.recommendation: Address rough running or starting issues promptly - injector problems rarely improve on their own. Use high-quality diesel fuel and change the fuel filter regularly to extend fuel system life. If the high-pressure pump has failed, have the entire fuel system flushed to prevent debris from damaging new components.
problems.cta: -> Compare Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D fuel system repair costs

problems.h4: Coolant Loss & EGR Cooler Failure - Why the Toyota Auris 1.4 D-4D 1ND-TV Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop leaks over time, causing gradual coolant loss without visible external leaks. If left unchecked, this can lead to overheating and potential head gasket failure. The challenge is distinguishing EGR cooler leaks from head gasket failure - a pressure test is recommended.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler with new OEM unit; refill and bleed cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution for EGR cooler leaks

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnose coolant loss source; identify EGR cooler vs head gasket

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £1,800-£2,200 (matches Section 4 rebuilt figure for this code)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit complete engine with new cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating has caused head gasket or cylinder damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For an Auris 1.4 D-4D worth £1,500-£5,000, EGR cooler replacement at £350-£650 is good value for restoring reliability. If overheating has occurred and the head gasket is compromised, evaluate repair costs carefully against vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of coolant loss without visible leaks, have a pressure test performed. Catching an EGR cooler leak early prevents overheating and much more expensive repairs. If you're replacing the EGR cooler, consider having the EGR valve cleaned at the same time.
